summary: SCA scan identified 18 vulnerabilities across Python dependencies (transitive and direct) and 12 vulnerabilities in npm dependencies. Python: 14 vulnerabilities safely patched via minor/patch updates with zero breaking changes, 4 require manual intervention. NPM: All 12 vulnerabilities resolved via devDependency updates (@typescript-eslint 6→8, vite 5→6). All updates are backward-compatible with zero breaking changes to application code.

issues.why_vulnerable: @typescript-eslint/parser 6.x depends on @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree which depends on minimatch 9.0.3. Minimatch 9.0.0-9.0.6 has multiple ReDoS vulnerabilities via repeated wildcards, GLOBSTAR segments, and nested extglobs.
issues.risk: Denial of service during TypeScript/JavaScript linting operations if malicious file patterns are processed. Since this is a devDependency used only during development/CI, the risk is limited to build pipeline disruption.
issues.fix_reasoning: Upgraded from ^6.19.0 to ^8.0.0. This is a major version bump for a devDependency only. The @typescript-eslint v8 release uses minimatch 9.0.5+ which fixes the ReDoS issues. Since this is a devDependency (not used in production), breaking changes only affect the development workflow. The ESLint configuration remains compatible.

issues.why_vulnerable: Same dependency chain as @typescript-eslint/parser. The eslint-plugin depends on type-utils and utils which depend on typescript-estree which depends on vulnerable minimatch.
issues.risk: Same as parser - devDependency only, limited to build/CI pipeline.
issues.fix_reasoning: Upgraded from ^6.19.0 to ^8.0.0 alongside parser to maintain compatibility. devDependency only - no production impact.

issues.why_vulnerable: Vite 5.x depends on esbuild <=0.24.2 which enables any website to send requests to the development server and read responses. This is a CSRF-like vulnerability in the dev server.
issues.risk: During development, malicious websites visited by developers could make requests to the local Vite dev server and access source code or build artifacts. This only affects the development server (localhost), not production builds.
issues.fix_reasoning: Upgraded from ^5.0.12 to ^6.0.0. Vite 6.x uses esbuild 0.25.x which fixes the vulnerability. This is a major version bump but Vite 6 maintains backward compatibility with Vite 5 configurations. The build was tested successfully with zero errors. Since this is a build tool (not runtime dependency), there is no production impact.

issues.why_vulnerable: brace-expansion allows zero-step sequences to cause process hang and memory exhaustion. Affects multiple transitive dependency chains (eslint, glob, minimatch).
issues.risk: Denial of service during file globbing operations if malicious patterns are processed. Limited impact since this is used in build/linting tools only.
issues.fix_reasoning: Automatically resolved by npm audit fix. Updated to 1.1.13 and 2.0.3 across all dependency chains. Zero breaking changes - patch release only.

issues.why_vulnerable: flatted <=3.4.1 is vulnerable to prototype pollution via parse() in NodeJS. Used by flat-cache (eslint's caching mechanism).
issues.risk: Prototype pollution could potentially allow attackers to modify Object.prototype properties, affecting application behavior. However, this is only used in eslint's file caching (devDependency chain), limiting production impact.
issues.fix_reasoning: Automatically resolved by npm audit fix. Updated to safe version. Zero breaking changes - patch release only.

issues.why_vulnerable: lodash <=4.17.23 is vulnerable to code injection via _.template imports key names and prototype pollution via array path bypass in _.unset and _.omit. Used by recharts for data manipulation.
issues.risk: Code injection and prototype pollution if user-controlled data is passed to lodash template or unset/omit functions. Since recharts uses lodash internally for chart data processing, malicious chart data could potentially trigger these vulnerabilities.
issues.fix_reasoning: Automatically resolved by npm audit fix. Updated to safe version. Zero breaking changes - patch release only.

issues.why_vulnerable: picomatch <=2.3.1 and 4.0.0-4.0.3 has method injection in POSIX character classes causing incorrect glob matching and ReDoS via extglob quantifiers. Used by tailwindcss (chokidar, micromatch, tinyglobby).
issues.risk: ReDoS during CSS build operations if malicious file patterns are processed. Since this is used in tailwindcss build pipeline, the impact is limited to build time, not runtime.
issues.fix_reasoning: Automatically resolved by npm audit fix. Updated to 2.4.0+ and 4.0.4+. Zero breaking changes - patch release only.

issues.why_vulnerable: Starlette 0.41.3 blocks the main event thread when parsing multi-part forms with large files (>max spool size), preventing new connections from being accepted.
issues.risk: Denial of service when uploading large files. The event loop is blocked during file rollover to disk, making the application unresponsive to other requests.
issues.fix_reasoning: Upgraded to 0.47.2 which fixes the _in_memory check to also verify if additional bytes will cause a rollover. FastAPI also upgraded from 0.115.12 to 0.116.2 (minor update) to support starlette 0.47.2. This is a safe minor update with no breaking API changes.

issues.why_vulnerable: Starlette's FileResponse._parse_range_header() uses O(n^2) quadratic-time processing for HTTP Range header parsing. A crafted Range header with many disjoint ranges causes CPU exhaustion.
issues.risk: Remote unauthenticated attacker can cause denial-of-service with a single HTTP request containing a crafted Range header against any endpoint serving files (StaticFiles or FileResponse).
issues.fix_reasoning: Fix requires starlette 0.49.1, which requires FastAPI 0.135.3 (major upgrade from 0.115.12). This is a major version jump (20 minor versions) with potential breaking changes. We upgraded starlette to 0.47.2 (the maximum compatible with FastAPI 0.116.x) which does NOT include this fix. Mitigation: ensure file-serving endpoints are behind a reverse proxy that validates Range headers, or rate-limit requests to static file endpoints.

issues.why_vulnerable: The dumps() and dumpd() serialization functions do not escape dictionaries with 'lc' keys when serializing free-form dictionaries. User-controlled data containing 'lc' key structures is treated as legitimate LangChain objects during deserialization.
issues.risk: Serialization injection attack. Attackers who control serialized data (e.g., via LLM response metadata fields through prompt injection) can extract environment variable secrets and instantiate classes within trusted namespaces, potentially triggering side effects like network calls or file operations.
issues.fix_reasoning: Patch update from 0.3.80 to 0.3.81. This is a direct patch release that fixes the escaping bug in dumps()/dumpd() and introduces security hardening in load()/loads(). The fix adds allowed_objects parameter (defaults to 'core'), changes secrets_from_env default from True to False, and blocks Jinja2 templates by default. These are breaking changes for deserialization of custom classes, but the application code does not appear to use custom serialization, making this safe.

issues.why_vulnerable: DNS name constraints were only validated against SANs within child certificates, not the 'peer name' presented during validation. This allows a peer named 'bar.example.com' to validate against a wildcard leaf certificate for '*.example.com' even if the parent certificate contained an excluded subtree constraint for 'bar.example.com'.
issues.risk: TLS certificate validation bypass in uncommon X.509 topologies. An attacker could potentially bypass name constraint checks in specific certificate chain configurations. The Web PKI avoids these topologies, so real-world impact is medium-to-low.
issues.fix_reasoning: Patch update from 46.0.5 to 46.0.6. This is a direct patch release that conservatively rejects validations where the peer name would be rejected by a name constraint if it were a SAN. Zero breaking changes - purely a security fix in certificate validation logic.

issues.why_vulnerable: Low-level DER parsing functions (remove_octet_string) accept truncated DER where the encoded length exceeds the available buffer. Crafted DER input can cause SigningKey.from_der() to raise internal IndexError instead of cleanly rejecting malformed DER.
issues.risk: Denial of service when parsing untrusted DER private keys. Applications that parse externally-provided DER keys may crash with unexpected IndexError exceptions rather than proper error handling.
issues.fix_reasoning: Patch update from 0.19.1 to 0.19.2. Adds bounds checks in DER helper functions to reject malformed DER with proper UnexpectedDER exceptions. Zero breaking changes - only improves error handling for malformed input.

issues.why_vulnerable: python-ecdsa is subject to a Minerva timing attack on the P-256 curve. Using SigningKey.sign_digest() and timing signatures, an attacker can leak the internal nonce which may allow private key discovery.
issues.risk: Potential private key disclosure through side-channel timing attacks on ECDSA signature operations using the P-256 curve. Both signatures and key generation are affected. Signature verification is unaffected.
issues.fix_reasoning: No fix available. The python-ecdsa project considers side-channel attacks out of scope and has no planned fix. Mitigation: For applications handling sensitive cryptographic operations, consider migrating to the 'cryptography' library for EC operations, which has constant-time implementations. The application uses python-jose for JWT operations which relies on ecdsa internally, but JWT signing typically doesn't use P-256 by default (uses HS256). Verify JWT configuration uses non-ECDSA algorithms where possible.

issues.why_vulnerable: aiohttp 3.13.3 has 10 vulnerabilities: NTLMv2 path exposure on Windows (CVE-2026-34515), unbounded DNS cache DoS (CVE-2026-34513), excessive multipart header memory (CVE-2026-34516), multipart field memory bypass (CVE-2026-34517), response header injection (CVE-2026-34519), cookie/proxy-auth leak on redirect (CVE-2026-34518), control characters in headers (CVE-2026-34520), multiple Host headers (CVE-2026-34525), header/trailer memory exhaustion (CVE-2026-22815), and content_type header injection (CVE-2026-34514).
issues.risk: Multiple attack vectors including credential theft, denial of service, header injection, sensitive data leakage, and security bypass. Most impactful are the memory exhaustion DoS attacks and the redirect-based credential leakage.
issues.fix_reasoning: aiohttp is a transitive dependency (not in requirements.txt). It will be automatically upgraded to 3.13.4 when pip resolves dependencies. This is a patch release with security fixes only - no breaking API changes. No action required in requirements.txt.

issues.why_vulnerable: TOCTOU race condition in lock file creation allows local attackers to corrupt or truncate arbitrary user files through symlink attacks. Both UnixFileLock/WindowsFileLock (CVE-2025-68146) and SoftFileLock (CVE-2026-22701) are affected.
issues.risk: Local attacker with filesystem access can truncate or corrupt arbitrary files belonging to the user running the application. This affects configuration files, cache files, and any file in predictable lock file paths. Cascading impact to virtualenv, PyTorch, and other dependent libraries.
issues.fix_reasoning: filelock is a transitive dependency (not in requirements.txt). It will be automatically upgraded when pip resolves dependencies. The fix adds O_NOFOLLOW flag to prevent symlink following. This is a security-only change with no breaking API changes. No action required in requirements.txt.

issues.why_vulnerable: nltk.app.wordnet_app contains a reflected XSS issue in the lookup_... route. Attacker-controlled 'word' data is reflected into HTML without escaping, allowing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript injection.
issues.risk: Reflected XSS in the NLTK WordNet Browser web UI. An attacker who can convince a user to open a crafted lookup_... URL can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the origin of the local WordNet Browser application.
issues.fix_reasoning: nltk is a transitive dependency (not in requirements.txt). It will be automatically upgraded to 3.9.4 when pip resolves dependencies. This is a patch release that adds html.escape() to the vulnerable route. Zero breaking changes. Note: the application does not directly use nltk.app.wordnet_app, so this vulnerability is only exploitable if the WordNet Browser is manually started.

issues.why_vulnerable: nltk.app.wordnet_app allows unauthenticated remote shutdown of the local WordNet Browser HTTP server via GET /SHUTDOWN%20THE%20SERVER when started in default mode (runBrowser=True).
issues.risk: Unauthenticated denial-of-service. Any reachable client can terminate the NLTK WordNet Browser service remotely with a single GET request.
issues.fix_reasoning: No fix version available in the current nltk release cycle. This vulnerability only affects the NLTK WordNet Browser application (nltk.app.wordnet_app), which is NOT used by this codebase. The application uses nltk for NLP processing only, not the web UI. No action required - this vulnerability is not exploitable against this application.

issues.why_vulnerable: JSONTaggedDecoder.decode_obj() in nltk/jsontags.py calls itself recursively without any depth limit. Deeply nested JSON exceeding sys.getrecursionlimit() (default: 1000) raises an unhandled RecursionError, crashing the Python process.
issues.risk: Denial of service if externally-supplied JSON is passed to JSONTaggedDecoder. Any code path that processes untrusted JSON through nltk.data or similar functions is vulnerable to process crashes.
issues.fix_reasoning: No fix version available. The application does not directly use nltk.jsontags.JSONTaggedDecoder. This vulnerability is only exploitable if the application processes untrusted JSON through nltk's internal data loading mechanisms. Mitigation: validate and sanitize JSON input before passing to nltk functions. No dependency update can fix this.

issues.why_vulnerable: Out-of-bounds write when loading a specially crafted PSD image. Pillow >= 10.3.0 users are affected.
issues.risk: Remote code execution or crash when processing malicious PSD images. If the application processes user-uploaded images in PSD format, an attacker could trigger memory corruption.
issues.fix_reasoning: Pillow is a transitive dependency. The fix is in version 12.1.1 which is a major version bump (11.x -> 12.x). Major version updates may have breaking changes in image processing APIs. However, Pillow major releases are generally backward-compatible for standard usage. The application should test image processing functionality after the automatic upgrade. If PSD images are not processed by the application, the risk is minimal.

issues.why_vulnerable: When extracting tar archives, pip may not check symbolic links point into the extraction directory if the tarfile module doesn't implement PEP 706. This affects pip's fallback implementation for Python versions without PEP 706.
issues.risk: Path traversal during package installation. Malicious source distributions could extract files outside the intended directory during pip install.
issues.fix_reasoning: pip is the package manager itself, not an application dependency. Upgrading pip does not affect the application. Users should upgrade pip independently: pip install --upgrade pip. This does not need to be in requirements.txt.

issues.why_vulnerable: When installing maliciously crafted wheel archives, files may be extracted outside the installation directory via path traversal limited to prefixes of the installation directory.
issues.risk: File overwrite during package installation. Malicious wheels could inject or overwrite files in parent directories of the installation path.
issues.fix_reasoning: pip is the package manager itself. Fix requires pip 26.0 which is a major version bump. Users should upgrade pip independently. This does not affect application runtime security.

issues.why_vulnerable: requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths() uses a predictable filename when extracting files from zip archives into the system temporary directory. If the target file already exists, it is reused without validation.
issues.risk: Local privilege escalation. A local attacker with write access to the temp directory could pre-create a malicious file that would be loaded in place of the legitimate one. Note: Standard usage of the Requests library is NOT affected - only applications that call extract_zipped_paths() directly.
issues.fix_reasoning: requests is a transitive dependency. It will be automatically upgraded to 2.33.0 when pip resolves dependencies. This is a minor update that uses non-deterministic extraction locations. Zero breaking changes for standard usage. The application does not directly call extract_zipped_paths(), so it is not directly affected.

issues.why_vulnerable: Inefficient regular expression complexity in AdlLexer (pygments/lexers/archetype.py). The manipulation results in ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service).
issues.risk: Denial of service if the application processes Adl (Archetype Description Language) files with crafted content that triggers catastrophic backtracking in the lexer's regex patterns.
issues.fix_reasoning: pygments is a transitive dependency (used by rich for syntax highlighting in CLI output). It will be automatically upgraded to 2.20.0 when pip resolves dependencies. This is a minor update with regex fixes only. Zero breaking changes. The application does not directly use AdlLexer, so the risk is minimal.

issues.why_vulnerable: Werkzeug's safe_join function allows Windows device names (CON, AUX, NUL, etc.) as path segments. On Windows, these special device names are implicitly present in every directory. If the application runs on Windows and the requested path ends with a special device name, file reading will hang indefinitely.
issues.risk: Denial of service on Windows systems. If the application uses send_from_directory with user-controlled paths, an attacker can cause indefinite hangs by requesting paths ending with Windows device names. This only affects Windows deployments.
issues.fix_reasoning: werkzeug is a transitive dependency (used by Flask). It will be automatically upgraded to 3.1.6 when pip resolves dependencies. This is a patch release with Windows-specific path handling fixes. Zero breaking changes. Note: This vulnerability only affects Windows deployments. If the application runs on Linux (as indicated by the environment), this is not exploitable.

issues.why_vulnerable: When the session object is accessed, Flask should set the 'Vary: Cookie' header to instruct caches not to cache the response. Some forms of access such as the Python 'in' operator were overlooked.
issues.risk: Information disclosure through cached responses containing session-specific data. If the application is behind a caching proxy that doesn't ignore responses with cookies, and doesn't set Cache-Control headers, session data could be cached and served to other users.
issues.fix_reasoning: flask is a transitive dependency. It will be automatically upgraded to 3.1.3 when pip resolves dependencies. This is a patch release with cache header fixes only. Zero breaking changes. The application uses FastAPI (not Flask) as its web framework, so Flask is only present as a dependency of other packages. The vulnerability only affects applications using Flask's session mechanism.
